newsitem.title: TURKEY: Erbakan doubles Turkish sell-off revenue forecast.
newsitem.headline: Erbakan doubles Turkish sell-off revenue forecast.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Thursday doubled the government's forecast of revenues from privatisation by the end of 1997 to $13 billion.
The new forecast came following a meeting of Turkey's High Board of Privatisation on Wednesday.

"We announced that we will carry out privatisation worth $6.5 billion by the end of 1997. Work yesterday showed that we will realise at least twice this amount," Erbakan told reporters ahead of a cabinet meeting.

The country's ten-year old privatisation programme has been stalled repeatedly by political opposition and legal obstacles. Turkey has raised some $3 billion through sell-offs since the programme started in 1986.

Sell-off revenues have in the past fallen far short of government forecasts, but the Islamist-led coalition under Erbakan has said privatisation is a priority in its aim to raise badly-needed revenues.
Erbakan also told reporters he expects interest rates to fall below 100 percent in the near term.
"Interest rates have dropped to the 105 percent level. In the near future they will drop below 100 percent," he said.
